runtime_boundary: Represents the self-operated Ollama runtime. Ollama Cloud, the hosted tier operated by the same organization, is a separate managed inference service record. The model library Ollama distributes is not part of this record.
model_management: Models are pulled, pushed, created from a Modelfile, copied, listed, and deleted through the CLI and REST API. Safetensors weights and adapters can be imported into the local store.
hardware_requirements: Documented NVIDIA support requires compute capability 5.0 or newer with driver 550 or newer; AMD support runs through ROCm; Apple silicon runs through Metal. Models that do not fit one accelerator are spread across available GPUs, and available memory governs how many models load concurrently.
operational_controls: Server environment variables govern loaded-model count, parallel requests per model, and queue depth. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES restricts GPU selection. Running models and versions are inspectable through the API.
strengths: Model lifecycle management is unusually complete for a local runner, covering pull, push, create, copy, import, and delete through both CLI and API.
Documents OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible endpoints alongside its native API, plus embeddings, tool calling, structured outputs, and vision.
Installers, container images, and hardware support are documented per platform with explicit driver and compute-capability floors.
tradeoffs: Concurrency is limited to parallel request slots and multiple loaded models; the documentation describes no continuous batching or distributed serving.
Documented accelerator coverage spans NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple silicon; Vulkan and Intel paths are not part of the published hardware support matrix.
Operational visibility is limited to running-model and version endpoints with no documented metrics endpoint.
license_note: The repository publishes a single MIT license file covering the runtime source.
